title: Test incremental load: full + incremental runs, verify no duplicates
description: Deploy changes to Fabric and run end-to-end validation: (1) full load with p_full_load=true, (2) incremental load with p_full_load=false and p_from_date set, (3) verify no duplicate records in silver_procurement and fact_procurement, (4) compare row counts and performance.
acceptanceCriteria: Full load produces correct baseline (matches previous full load row counts)
Incremental load adds only new/changed records
No duplicates in silver_procurement or fact_procurement after incremental run
Full-vs-incremental runtime recorded and broken out by stage (bronze / silver / gold), stating the measured delta whatever it is — bronze is expected to show no saving.
incremental_load_strategy.md updated with actual performance numbers

Data wall-clock 22m25s -> 20m19s (-9%). WARM-CACHE CONFOUND: full load (step 1) was first run after capacity idle (cold Spark pool); incremental runs (3b/3c) reused warm pool — the bronze -64% is environmental, not incremental. Corroborating warm-held-constant comparison (3b empty-window vs 3c 22-row, both warm): silver 2m35s -> 3m37s (22 rows added ~1m02s), gold 10m38s -> 11m8s (22 rows added ~30s) — isolates the procurement delete-insert cost from warm-cache: ~1m silver, ~30s gold, confirming gold is full-scope-bound. AC4 HONEST READ: incremental saving is modest because only the procurement path is incremental; bronze shows no incremental saving (the -64% is warm-cache); gold shows no saving (full-scope-bound). This is the "state the measured delta whatever it is" AC4 result.
